title: DRRM Preparedness & Adaptation

competencies.text: Develop family and community-based DRRM plans.

days.title: What Is DRRM?
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will develop family and community-based disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM) plans.

🛡️ Disaster Risk Reduction and Management

DRRM is the organized way of preventing, reducing and coping with disaster risk. The Philippine DRRM Act of 2010 (RA 10121) shifted the country from simply responding after disasters to reducing risk before they happen. It created the NDRRMC and DRRM offices and councils down to the barangay level.

Thematic areaFocusExamples
1. Prevention and MitigationAvoid or lessen hazard impactsHazard maps, building codes, reforestation, drainage, mangroves
2. PreparednessBe ready to actDrills, early warning systems, Go Bags, evacuation plans
3. ResponseSave lives during and right afterEvacuation, search and rescue, first aid, relief
4. Rehabilitation and RecoveryRebuild betterRepairing homes and schools, restoring livelihoods, psychosocial support

Risk = Hazard × Exposure × Vulnerability ÷ Capacity. DRRM lowers exposure and vulnerability and raises capacity.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: Which law institutionalized DRRM in the Philippines?
scenario.explanation: RA 10121 is the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010.

scenario.text: Planting mangroves to reduce storm-surge damage belongs to which thematic area?
scenario.explanation: Mangroves lessen the impact of a hazard before it strikes — prevention and mitigation.

scenario.text: How can a community LOWER its disaster risk even if the hazard stays the same?

choices.label: Wait until the hazard becomes weaker
Move the hazard to another region

scenario.explanation: Risk depends on vulnerability and capacity as well as the hazard; strong houses, warnings and drills reduce risk.

days.title: The Family DRRM Plan
days.content:
👨‍👩‍👧 Parts of a Family Plan

  1. Know your hazards — check HazardHunterPH or barangay hazard maps for floods, landslides, faults, storm surge.
  2. Communication plan — emergency numbers, an out-of-town contact, and what to do if phone lines fail.
  3. Meeting points — one near home and one outside the neighborhood.
  4. Evacuation route — the nearest evacuation center and a safe path to it.
  5. Roles — who turns off power and gas, who helps the elderly, children and persons with disabilities, who brings pets.
  6. Go Bag — ready for 72 hours.
  7. Practice — drill the plan and update it yearly.

🎒 Go Bag Essentials

Drinking water, ready-to-eat food, flashlight and batteries, battery or crank radio, first-aid kit and maintenance medicines, whistle, copies of IDs and documents in a waterproof bag, some cash, hygiene items, face masks, extra clothes, and a power bank.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each term to its description. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Organized way to reduce and manage disaster risk
match.why: It covers before, during and after.

match.right: Be ready to act when a hazard comes
Save lives during and right after

match.why: Keep it ready near the exit.
It created DRRM councils at all levels.

days.title: The Community DRRM Plan
days.content:
🏘️ Barangay-Level DRRM

The Barangay DRRM Committee (BDRRMC) leads local planning. A good community plan includes:

  • Risk assessment and hazard mapping with residents' knowledge of past floods and landslides.
  • Early warning system — sirens, bells, text blasts, and clear signals understood by everyone.
  • Evacuation centers that are safe from hazards, with water, toilets, and spaces for women, children and the elderly.
  • Inclusive planning — lists of persons with disabilities, senior citizens, pregnant women and infants so no one is left behind.
  • Pre-emptive evacuation before a hazard arrives, not during it.
  • Drills — such as the Nationwide Simultaneous Earthquake Drill.

🏫 Schools

Under DepEd, every school has a DRRM coordinator, evacuation plans, and conducts drills. Students can help by mapping hazards around school and teaching families what they learn.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Apply DRRM planning. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: A Signal No. 3 typhoon will arrive in 24 hours. What should your family do FIRST?

choices.label: Review the plan, ready the Go Bag, heed evacuation advice
Wait until the winds are strong before deciding what to do
Go to the beach to see how big the waves are getting
Use all the stored water now so it will not go to waste

scenario.explanation: Acting early — reviewing the plan, preparing supplies and evacuating if advised — is the core of preparedness.

scenario.text: Which item should NEVER be left out of a Go Bag?
scenario.explanation: Safe drinking water is essential for survival during the first 72 hours.

scenario.text: Why is it important to join barangay earthquake drills?

choices.label: Drills stop earthquakes from happening in the barangay
Drills are only for teachers and barangay officials
Joining drills replaces the need for any family plan

scenario.explanation: Under stress, people do what they have practiced. Drills build the habits that save lives.

scenario.text: Your grandmother uses a wheelchair. How should she be included in the family plan?

choices.label: Assign a helper and plan an accessible route early
Leave her at home since she cannot use the stairs alone
Ask her to evacuate last, after everyone else
Wait for rescuers to arrive after the disaster

scenario.explanation: Inclusive plans assign responsibilities and plan for early, accessible evacuation of people with mobility needs.

scenario.text: A coastal barangay sets a rule to evacuate low areas when a storm surge warning is issued, even before rain begins. What is this called?
scenario.explanation: Moving people out before the hazard arrives is pre-emptive evacuation, a preparedness measure.

days.title: Adapting for the Future
days.content:
🔗 DRRM Meets Climate Change Adaptation

Climate change makes some hazards stronger and more frequent — intense rainfall, stronger typhoons, higher storm surges and more dangerous heat. So DRRM plans must look ahead, not just at past disasters:

  • Use projections of sea-level rise and rainfall when planning roads, schools and houses.
  • Build back better after disasters — stronger, safer and in less exposed locations.
  • Protect ecosystems (mangroves, forests, reefs) as natural defenses.
  • Diversify livelihoods so families recover faster after crop or fishing losses.

🧠 Your Role

Young people can map hazards, share PAGASA and PHIVOLCS warnings with family, help prepare Go Bags, and volunteer in barangay activities. A prepared family is the foundation of a resilient community.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.explanation: DRRM means Disaster Risk Reduction and Management.

escape.text: How many thematic areas does the national DRRM framework have?
escape.explanation: Prevention and Mitigation, Preparedness, Response, and Rehabilitation and Recovery.

escape.text: Which thematic area includes drills, Go Bags and evacuation plans?
escape.explanation: Preparedness gets people and systems ready to act before a hazard strikes.

escape.text: Which activity is an example of MITIGATION?

choices.label: Following building codes for earthquake-resistant homes
Distributing relief goods after a typhoon has passed
Rescuing families trapped on their roofs during a flood
Giving counseling to survivors a month after a disaster

escape.explanation: Building to code lessens damage before a hazard strikes — mitigation. The others are response or recovery.

escape.text: Why should evacuation happen BEFORE a typhoon arrives?

choices.label: Travel gets dangerous once winds and floods start
Evacuation centers are always closed during typhoons
Typhoons always pass faster than forecast
Families can only evacuate in the daytime

escape.explanation: Strong winds, flying debris and rising water make late evacuation risky for both residents and rescuers.

escape.text: What does "build back better" mean in recovery?

choices.label: Rebuild stronger and safer than before
Rebuild exactly as it was before
Rebuild only the barangay hall first
Do not rebuild anything after a disaster

escape.explanation: Recovery should reduce future risk — stronger structures, safer locations and better systems.
